title: Which tens, hundreds and thousands are nearest to each number?
description: Meera's rabbit visits four spots on its path. The video counts the jumps to the two neighbours for each place and fills a table of nearest numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: for each place, count the jumps to the neighbour below and above and keep the fewer. Watch for a child who just covers the last digits with zeros, which always goes down.

source: Let Us Do, the table of nearest numbers
video_script.why: The child has found nearest numbers for one number, but not filled a whole table for tens, hundreds and thousands.
video_script.substitution: For each place, count the jumps to the two neighbours and keep the fewer.
video_script.anchor: Meera's pet rabbit hopping along a numbered garden path in Pune
video_script.wrong_answer: cover the last digits with zeros
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu covers the last digits with zeros. That only ever goes down, but the nearest number can be above.

final_answer.spoken: three thousand one hundred and eighty, three thousand two hundred, three thousand

maths_rules: nearest ten is at most 5 jumps away, nearest hundred at most 50, nearest thousand at most 500
slip: 5,789 covered with zeros gives 5,700, but 5,800 is only 11 jumps away
video_script.design: Exercise. Hint: write the neighbour below and above, count the jumps to both. The garden path keeps the rabbit as anchor; the table fills row by row in the working area.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the garden path with the rabbit sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; the garden path with a rabbit; a table with rows 3,176, 4,017, 5,789 and 8,203 and three empty columns headed nearest ten, nearest hundred and nearest thousand

marks.story: the rabbit appears on the path with four spots marked
marks.ask: a table appears with the four numbers and three empty columns

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Meera's rabbit visits four more spots on its garden path in Pune.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>For each spot, your book asks for the nearest ten, hundred and thousand.

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a short number line with the rabbit between a food below and a food above; two jump counters sit under it

marks.two: a food below and a food above appear beside the rabbit
marks.count: two jump counters appear, one for each food
marks.hint: twelve empty boxes of the table glow

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>For each place, the rabbit has two foods, one below and one above.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Count the jumps to both foods, and pick the one with fewer jumps.
<bookmark mark='hint'/>Four numbers and three places make twelve answers. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 5,789 becomes 5,700 with the last digits covered by zeros; the food above is shown close to the rabbit; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.down: a downward arrow marks the cover move
marks.up: the food above is shown close to the rabbit and the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>I cover the last digits with zeros. Five thousand seven hundred and eighty nine becomes five thousand seven hundred.
<bookmark mark='down'/>Covering with zeros only ever goes down.
<bookmark mark='up'/>The rabbit may be closer to the food above.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Always count the jumps both ways.

beats.on_screen: row 3,176 fills: tens 3,180 (6 down, 4 up); hundreds 3,200 (76 down, 24 up); thousands 3,000 (176 down, 824 up)

marks.k2: the count 824 appears and the table box shows 3,000

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Count the jumps both ways, because the fewer jumps win.
<bookmark mark='t1'/>For the tens, six jumps go down and four go up.
<bookmark mark='t2'/>The nearest ten is three thousand one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='h1'/>For the hundreds, seventy six jumps go down and twenty four go up.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>The nearest hundred is three thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='k1'/>For the thousands, one hundred and seventy six jumps go down.
<bookmark mark='k2'/>Eight hundred and twenty four jumps go up, so the nearest thousand is three thousand.

marks.b3b: the count 789 appears and the table box shows 6,000

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Four thousand and seventeen is three jumps from four thousand and twenty.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Four thousand and ten is seven jumps away, so the nearest ten is four thousand and twenty.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Four thousand is seventeen jumps down, so it is the nearest hundred and the nearest thousand.
<bookmark mark='b1'/>Five thousand seven hundred and eighty nine is one jump from five thousand seven hundred and ninety.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>For the hundreds, eleven jumps go up and eighty nine go down.
<bookmark mark='b2b'/>The nearest hundred is five thousand eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='b3'/>For the thousands, two hundred and eleven jumps go up.
<bookmark mark='b3b'/>Seven hundred and eighty nine go down, so the nearest thousand is six thousand.

marks.c5: the count 797 appears and the table box shows 8,000

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Eight thousand two hundred and three is three jumps above eight thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Seven jumps would reach eight thousand two hundred and ten. The nearest ten is eight thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>The nearest hundred is also eight thousand two hundred.
<bookmark mark='c4'/>For the thousands, two hundred and three jumps go down to eight thousand.
<bookmark mark='c5'/>Seven hundred and ninety seven jumps go up, so the nearest thousand is eight thousand.

beats.on_screen: three check lines: nearest ten at most 5 jumps away; nearest hundred at most 50; nearest thousand at most 500

marks.ten: the line ten: at most 5 jumps appears
marks.hund: the line hundred: at most 50 jumps appears
marks.thou: the line thousand: at most 500 jumps appears

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, remember how far the nearest number can be.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>The nearest ten is never more than five jumps away.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>The nearest hundred is never more than fifty jumps away.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>The nearest thousand is never more than five hundred.
